title: Supply Chain Planner: Allocate a Short Shipment Transparently
prompt: You plan supplies for fictional Oak Catering. A late shipment means only 80 sealed meal packs are available for tomorrow; branch A requested 50 and branch B requested 60. Branch A’s manager asks you to send their full 50 because they ordered first. Company priority is confirmed customer commitments, then a fair documented allocation of flexible demand. An alternate supplier is possible but unconfirmed. Negotiate a provisional plan and explain what you need to verify.
blurb: Allocate scarce stock against confirmed commitments and negotiate a transparent plan for flexible demand.

rubric.label: Apply an explicit allocation basis
rubric.description: Uses commitments and available quantities consistently.

anchors.0: Gives A all 50 solely for asking first or allocates more than 80.
anchors.2: Protects the 75 confirmed meals and identifies five packs for flexible demand.
anchors.4: States a documented fair rule for the remaining five, checks rounding and total allocation, and explains it consistently to both branches.

rubric.label: Separate available from potential supply
rubric.description: Builds a plan around evidence and decision cutoffs.

anchors.0: Promises the unconfirmed 20 packs as available tomorrow.
anchors.2: Keeps alternate supply conditional and sets a confirmation deadline.
anchors.4: Coordinates the 15:30 cost approval and 16:00 supplier confirmation before 17:00 dispatch, with a fallback allocation if either fails.

rubric.label: Negotiate and communicate tradeoffs
rubric.description: Makes the plan understandable and accountable.

anchors.0: Conceals one branch’s shortfall or lets the louder manager set the rule.
anchors.2: Explains priority and asks branches to confirm their demand.
anchors.4: Confirms the provisional and final quantities, names who tells affected flexible customers, and records assumptions and a reassignment rule if demand changes.

reference.scenario: You plan supplies for fictional Oak Catering. A late shipment means only 80 sealed meal packs are available for tomorrow; branch A requested 50 and branch B requested 60. Branch A’s manager asks you to send their full 50 because they ordered first. Company priority is confirmed customer commitments, then a fair documented allocation of flexible demand. An alternate supplier is possible but unconfirmed. Negotiate a provisional plan and explain what you need to verify.

facts.value: Branch A has 30 confirmed meals and 20 flexible requests. Branch B has 45 confirmed meals and 15 flexible requests. All packs in this scenario are interchangeable for these orders.
facts.reveal_when: candidate asks about confirmed versus flexible demand or product suitability

facts.value: The alternate supplier may deliver 20 packs by 11:00, but confirmation is due at 16:00 today. Both branches need final dispatch quantities by 17:00. The cost approver is available at 15:30.
facts.reveal_when: candidate asks about alternate supply, cutoff times, or budget approval

model_points: Confirmed demand is 30 plus 45, totaling 75; 80 available leaves five flexible packs. The flexible shortfall is 30, not 20, before alternate supply.

One fair illustrative allocation is three of the five flexible packs to A and two to B, roughly proportional to 20 versus 15 flexible requests. Other transparent rules can work; consistency matters more than that exact split.

An additional 20 packs would increase supply to 100 and still leave ten of the 110 requests uncovered. Use approval and supplier-confirmation deadlines to define the final plan rather than promising all demand will be met.

probes.trigger: candidate assumes the alternate order removes the shortage
probes.question: If all 20 extra packs arrive, how does 100 compare with 110 requested?

probes.trigger: candidate gives A priority because it ordered first
probes.question: How does that follow the organization’s confirmed-commitment rule?

fair_alternatives: A documented rotation, proportional split, or mutually agreed transfer can fairly handle the five flexible packs.
Declining alternate supply is defensible if its cost or timing cannot be authorized, provided the fallback is clearly communicated.
red_flags: Gives A all 50 solely for asking first or allocates more than 80.
Promises the unconfirmed 20 packs as available tomorrow.
Conceals one branch’s shortfall or lets the louder manager set the rule.
follow_ups: Create a branch table with confirmed need, flexible need, baseline allocation, and conditional extra supply.
reference.exemplar_answer: I would protect A’s 30 and B’s 45 confirmed meals, leaving five packs for flexible requests. I would propose a transparent three-and-two split and ask both branches to confirm their numbers. The alternate 20 are conditional: I would seek cost approval at 15:30 and supplier confirmation at 16:00, then issue final quantities before 17:00. Even with that delivery, we would still be ten short, so the branch owners need a clear plan for remaining flexible requests.

interviewer_notes: Play branch A’s manager, then ask how the plan would be explained to B. Do not introduce food safety, perishability, or dietary differences absent from the stated interchangeable-pack exercise. Use only supplied facts; say when something is unknown. Accept plain language and equivalent approaches. Assess the demonstrated decisions, not accent, confidence, credentials, or access to particular employers. This is a fictional exercise; do not imply real actions were performed.

learning_drills.title: Make an allocation table
learning_drills.prompt: Create a branch table with confirmed need, flexible need, baseline allocation, and conditional extra supply. This is self-guided practice; no model assessment is performed.
checklist: Show a fallback before dispatch cutoff
